beats.headline: The dungeon's pokeball
beats.text: Donut has trained Mongo to perch quietly on her back, clinging to her fur, and he has behaved himself. Mostly. Odette has mentioned something called a magical pet carrier, apparently the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball. They are supposedly expensive, but one would let them put a bonded pet into inventory without harming him. Carl doesn't care how much it costs. If they can afford it, it is going to be one of their first purchases.

beats.headline: Fifteen thousand gold
beats.text: They spend 15,000 gold on a magical pet carrier for Mongo. Neither Donut nor Mongo is keen, but Mordecai points out that the dinosaur feels obliged to guard them while they sleep, even in a safe room, and it is hurting his stats; and no pets are allowed in the Desperado Club. The device is a square brown box the size of a Rubik's Cube with a fire hydrant etched on the outside. Donut activates it, Mongo is zapped inside to sleep and regain his strength, and a press of the button calls him back out.

beats.headline: It doesn't work
beats.text: A door glows behind them, locked until the fight is over, and Mongo is hurt. Donut is more taken up with him than with the fight. He no longer seems to be in pain, but he is bleeding. Carl, Mongo won't stop bleeding, she cries. My pet carrier doesn't work! His health is still going down. Carl tosses a broken side table onto the stairs and tells her to try one of the bandages. They each have hundreds of them.

beats.headline: Ren's parting gift
beats.text: Ren gives Carl her best gear, and Garret: unconscious, level one now, his name gone, a tiny round ball on two stubby legs with a single tooth sticking out. She picks him up, kisses him, says she is sorry, and puts him in a pet carrier. His new weakness, she adds, is something called Reaper Gaze. She slides the carrier across, and before he can talk himself out of it Carl puts it in his inventory. A host of pet-themed achievements appear and disappear.

beats.headline: Keep him boxed up
beats.text: Carl asks Mordecai what to do with the tummy acher. Keep that thing in your inventory, Mordecai says. Carl couldn't go down the stairs with Mongo before because he didn't have a pet carrier. This one will be fine as long as he stays boxed up. Bonding can wait: with everything else on Carl's plate, a level-one pet is too much to keep alive, especially if it has an undead weakness. And Ren made a mistake saying his weaknesses out loud.
